statements.subject: nntp
statements.description: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119 [RFC2119].

statements.subject: nntp
statements.description: An implementation is not compliant if it fails to satisfy one or more of the MUST requirements for this protocol.

statements.subject: nntp
statements.description: An implementation that satisfies all the MUST and all the SHOULD requirements for its protocols is said to be "unconditionally compliant"; one that satisfies all the MUST requirements but not all the SHOULD requirements for NNTP is said to be "conditionally compliant".

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the argument does not meet the requirements of that section (for example, if it does not fit the grammar of Section 4.1), the NNTP server MAY place some interpretation on it (not specified by this document) or otherwise MUST treat it as a syntax error.

statements.subject: nntp
statements.description: A "keyword" MUST consist only of US-ASCII letters, digits, and the characters dot (".") and dash ("-") and MUST begin with a letter.

statements.subject: nntp
statements.description: Keywords MUST be at least three characters in length.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When the connection is established, the NNTP server host MUST send a greeting.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When a client host wishes to make use of the service, it MUST establish a TCP connection with the server host by connecting to that host on the same port on which the server is listening.
actions: establish TCP connection to server listening port

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Commands in NNTP MUST consist of a keyword, which MAY be followed by one or more arguments.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: A CRLF pair MUST terminate all commands.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Multiple commands MUST NOT be on the same line.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Unless otherwise noted elsewhere in this document, arguments SHOULD consist of printable US-ASCII characters.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Keywords and arguments MUST each be separated by one or more space or TAB characters.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Command lines MUST NOT exceed 512 octets, which includes the terminating CRLF pair.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The arguments MUST NOT exceed 497 octets.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MAY relax these limits for commands defined in an extension.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Where this specification permits UTF-8 characters outside the range of U+0000 to U+007F, implementations MUST NOT use the Byte Order Mark (U+FEFF, encoding %xEF.BB.BF) and MUST use the Word Joiner (U+2060, encoding %xE2.91.A0) for the meaning Zero Width No-Break Space in command lines and the initial lines of responses.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Implementations SHOULD apply these same principles throughout.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Keywords are case insensitive; the case of keywords for commands MUST be ignored by the server.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Each response MUST start with a three-digit response code that is sufficient to distinguish all responses.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The initial line of the response MUST NOT exceed 512 octets, which includes the response code and the terminating CRLF pair; an extension MAY specify a greater maximum for commands that it defines, but not for any other command.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: An NNTP server MAY have an inactivity autologout timer.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: Such a timer SHOULD be of at least three minutes' duration, with the exception that there MAY be a shorter limit on how long the server is willing to wait for the first command from the client.
actions: optionally configure shorter initial-command wait limit

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The receipt of any command from the client during the timer interval SHOULD suffice to reset the autologout timer.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: Similarly, the receipt of any significant amount of data from a client that is sending a multi-line data block (such as during a POST or IHAVE command) SHOULD suffice to reset the autologout timer.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When the timer expires, the server SHOULD close the connection without sending any response to the client.
actions: do not send response to client

statements.subject: message
statements.description: It MUST adhere to the following rules:

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Apart from those line endings, the stream MUST NOT include the octets NUL, LF, or CR.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If any line of the data block begins with the "termination octet" ("." or %x2E), that line MUST be "dot-stuffed" by prepending an additional termination octet to that line of the block.

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: The lines of the block MUST be followed by a terminating line consisting of a single termination octet followed by a CRLF pair in the normal way.
actions: append terminating line ('.' CRLF) to signal end of multi-line block

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: When a multi-line block is interpreted, the "dot-stuffing" MUST be undone; i.e., the recipient MUST ensure that, in any line beginning with the termination octet followed by octets other than a CRLF pair, that initial termination octet is disregarded.
actions: undo dot-stuffing when interpreting multi-line block

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: Likewise, the terminating line ("." CRLF or %x2E.0D.0A) MUST NOT be considered part of the multi-line block; i.e., the recipient MUST ensure that any line beginning with the termination octet followed immediately by a CRLF pair is disregarded.
actions: exclude terminating line from multi-line block content

statements.subject: message
statements.description: However, except when stated otherwise, this specification does not require the content to be UTF-8, and therefore (subject to that same requirement) it MAY include octets above and below 128 mixed arbitrarily.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Each response MUST begin with a three-digit status indicator.

statements.subject: nntp
statements.description: Any extension MUST follow this principle as well.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In all other cases, the client MUST only use the status indicator itself to determine the nature of the response.
actions: parse three-digit numeric status indicator from received response
determine nature of response (single-line vs multi-line, argument count) from status indicator only

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Arguments MUST be separated from the numeric status indicator and from each other by a single space.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: All numeric arguments MUST be in base 10 (decimal) format and MAY have leading zeros.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: String arguments MUST contain at least one character and MUST NOT contain TAB, LF, CR, or space.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MAY add any text after the response code or last argument, as appropriate, and the client MUST NOT make decisions based on this text.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Such text MUST be separated from the numeric status indicator or the last argument by at least one space.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST respond to any command with the appropriate generic response (given in Section 3.2.1) if it represents the situation.
actions: send the applicable generic response as defined in Section 3.2.1

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Otherwise, each recognized command MUST return one of the response codes specifically listed in its description or in an extension.
statements.post_cond: response.code in command.listed_codes | response.code in extension.listed_codes
actions: return one of the response codes listed in the command description or applicable extension

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MAY provide extensions to this specification, including new commands, new variants or features of existing commands, and other ways of changing the internal state of the server.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: However, the server MUST NOT produce any other responses to a client that does not invoke any of the additional features.
actions: restrict responses to those defined in this specification only

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If a client receives an unexpected response, it SHOULD use the first digit of the response to determine the result.
actions: use the first digit of the response code to classify the result (e.g. 2xx=success, 4xx/5xx=failure)

statements.subject: nntp
statements.description: Response codes not specified in this document MAY be used for any installation-specific additional commands also not specified.

statements.subject: nntp
statements.description: These SHOULD be chosen to fit the pattern of x9x specified above.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST respond to any command with the appropriate one of the following generic responses if it represents the situation.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the command is not recognized, or if it is an optional command that is not implemented by the server, the response code 500 MUST be returned.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If there is a syntax error in the arguments of a recognized command, including the case where more arguments are provided than the command specifies or the command line is longer than the server accepts, the response code 501 MUST be returned.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The line MUST NOT be truncated or split and then interpreted.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Note that where a command has variants depending on a second keyword (e.g., LIST ACTIVE and LIST NEWSGROUPS), 501 MUST be used when the base command is implemented but the requested variant is not, and 500 MUST be used only when the base command itself is not implemented.
statements.post_cond: (command.base.implemented = true & command.variant.implemented = false & response.code = 501) | (command.base.implemented = false & response.code = 500)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If an argument is required to be a base64-encoded string [RFC4648] (there are no such arguments in this specification, but there may be in extensions) and is not validly encoded, the response code 504 MUST be returned.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server experiences an internal fault or problem that means it is unable to carry out the command (for example, a necessary file is missing or a necessary service could not be contacted), the response code 403 MUST be returned.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server recognizes the command but does not provide an optional feature (for example, because it does not store the required information), or if it only handles a subset of legitimate cases (see the HDR command, Section 8.5, for an example), the response code 503 MUST be returned.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the client is not authorized to use the specified facility when the server is in its current state, then the appropriate one of the following response codes MUST be used.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Historically, some mode-switching servers (see Section 3.4.1) used this response to indicate that this command will become available after the MODE READER command (Section 5.3) is used, but this usage does not conform to this specification and MUST NOT be used.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Note that the server MUST NOT close the connection immediately after a 502 response except at the initial connection (Section 5.1) and with the MODE READER command.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The first argument of the response MUST be the capability label (see Section 5.2) of the facility that provides the necessary mechanism (usually an extension, which may be a private extension).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST NOT use this response code except as specified by the definition of the capability in question.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server has to terminate the connection for some reason, it MUST give a 400 response code to the next command and then immediately close the connection.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Following a 400 response, clients SHOULD NOT simply reconnect immediately and retry the same actions.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Rather, a client SHOULD either use an exponentially increasing delay between retries (e.g., double the waiting time after each 400 response) or present any associated text to the user for them to decide whether and when to retry.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MUST be prepared to receive any of these responses for any command (except, of course, that the server MUST NOT generate a 500 response code for mandatory commands).

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Each capability line consists of one or more tokens, which MUST be separated by one or more space or TAB characters.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST ensure that the capability list accurately reflects the capabilities (including extensions) currently available.
actions: Return a capability list that accurately reflects all capabilities and extensions currently available

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a capability is only available with the server in a certain state (for example, only after authentication), the list MUST only include the capability label when the server is in that state.
actions: Include capability label in capability list only when server is in the state where that capability is available
Omit capability label from capability list when server is not in the required state

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Similarly, if only some of the commands in an extension will be available, or if the behaviour of the extension will change in some other manner, according to the state of the server, this MUST be indicated by different arguments in the capability line.
actions: Emit different capability line arguments to reflect state-dependent extension availability or behavioral changes

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In order to interoperate with such versions, clients MUST be prepared to receive lines beginning with other characters and MUST ignore any they do not understand.
actions: Accept capability response lines beginning with non-letter characters without aborting processing
Ignore any capability lines that the client does not understand

statements.subject: server
statements.description: This capability MUST be advertised by all servers and MUST be the first capability in the capability list; it indicates the version(s) of NNTP that the server supports.
actions: include VERSION capability in capability list response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: There must be at least one argument; each argument is a decimal number and MUST NOT have a leading zero.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Version numbers are assigned only in RFCs that update or replace this specification; servers MUST NOT create their own version numbers.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: There MUST be one argument for each variant of the LIST command supported by the server, giving the keyword for that variant.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: This capability MAY be provided by a server.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If so, the arguments SHOULD be used to provide information such as the server software name and version number.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MUST NOT use this line to determine capabilities of the server.
actions: do not derive server capability set from IMPLEMENTATION capability line

statements.subject: nntp
statements.description: Each extension MUST define at least one new capability label (this will often, but need not, be the name of one of these new commands).

statements.subject: nntp
statements.description: While any additional capability information can normally be specified using arguments to that label, an extension MAY define more than one capability label.

statements.subject: nntp
statements.description: However, this SHOULD be limited to exceptional circumstances.

statements.subject: nntp
statements.description: the capability label or labels defined by the extension (the capability label of a registered extension MUST NOT begin with "X").

statements.subject: nntp
statements.description: Any new NNTP commands associated with the extension (the names of commands associated with registered extensions MUST NOT begin with "X").

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A private extension MAY or MAY NOT be included in the capabilities list.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If it is, the capability label MUST begin with "X".

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MAY provide additional keywords (for new commands and also for new variants of existing commands) as part of a private extension.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: To avoid the risk of a clash with a future registered extension, these keywords SHOULD begin with "X".

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server advertises a capability defined by a registered extension, it MUST implement the extension so as to fully conform with the specification (for example, it MUST implement all the commands that the extension describes as mandatory).
actions: implement the registered extension in full conformance with its specification
implement all commands that the extension specification describes as mandatory

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If it does not implement the extension as specified, it MUST NOT list the extension in the capabilities list under its registered name.
actions: omit the registered extension name from the capabilities list response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In that case, it MAY, but SHOULD NOT, provide a private extension (not listed, or listed with a different name) that implements part of the extension or implements the commands of the extension with a different meaning.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MUST NOT send different response codes to basic NNTP commands documented here or to commands documented in registered extensions in response to the availability or use of a private extension.
actions: send only the standard response codes defined for the invoked NNTP command regardless of private extension availability or use

statements.subject: nntp
statements.description: All capability labels in the registry MUST be keywords and MUST NOT begin with X.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the label is included in the capability list returned by the server, the server MUST support all commands in that bundle.
actions: Support all commands belonging to the bundle indicated by the advertised capability label

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the label is not included, the server MAY support none or some of the commands but SHOULD NOT support all of them.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Where a server does not implement a command, it MUST always generate a 500 generic response code (or a 501 generic response code in the case of a variant of a command depending on a second keyword where the base command is recognised).
statements.post_cond: (command.is_variant = false & response.code = 500) | (command.is_variant = true & command.base_recognised = true & response.code = 501)
actions: Send 500 response code when the command is not implemented
Send 501 response code when the unimplemented command is a variant whose base command is recognised

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Otherwise, the command MUST be fully implemented as specified; a server MUST NOT only partially implement any of the commands in this specification.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the former command is implemented but the latter is not, the former MUST still generate the relevant specific response code.
actions: Generate the relevant specific response code indicating the unmet prerequisite state (e.g., 412 when ARTICLE is implemented but GROUP is not)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Except as an effect of the MODE READER command (Section 5.3) on a mode-switching server, once a server advertises either or both of the IHAVE or READER capabilities, it MUST continue to advertise them for the entire session.
actions: maintain advertisement of IHAVE capability for entire session
maintain advertisement of READER capability for entire session

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MAY provide different modes of behaviour (transit, reader, or a combination) to different client connections and MAY use external information, such as the IP address of the client, to determine which mode to provide to any given connection.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: However, if a host wishes to offer separate servers for transit and reading clients, port 433 SHOULD be used for the transit server and 119 for the reading server.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: An implementation MAY, but SHOULD NOT, provide both transit and reader facilities on the same server but require the client to select which it wishes to use.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: It MUST advertise the MODE-READER capability.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: It MUST NOT advertise the READER capability.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: However, the server MAY cease to advertise the MODE-READER capability after the client uses any command except CAPABILITIES.
statements.trigger: client issues command other than CAPABILITIES

statements.subject: server
statements.description: It MUST NOT advertise the MODE-READER capability.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: It MUST advertise the READER capability.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: It MAY NOT advertise the IHAVE capability, even if it was advertising it in transit mode.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client SHOULD only issue a MODE READER command to a server if it is advertising the MODE-READER capability.
actions: issue MODE READER command only when server advertises MODE-READER capability

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the server does not support CAPABILITIES (and therefore does not conform to this specification), the client MAY use the following heuristic:

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client wishes to use any "reader" commands, it SHOULD use the MODE READER command immediately after the initial connection.
statements.trigger: client wishes to use reader commands
actions: send MODE READER command immediately after initial connection

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Otherwise, it SHOULD NOT use the MODE READER command.
actions: do not send MODE READER command

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Except where stated otherwise, a client MAY use pipelining.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST allow pipelining and MUST NOT throw away any text received after a command.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Irrespective of whether pipelining is used, the server MUST process commands in the order they are sent.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If the specific description of a command says it "MUST NOT be pipelined", that command MUST end any pipeline of commands.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: That is, the client MUST NOT send any following command until it receives the CRLF at the end of the response from the command.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MAY ignore any data received after the command and before the CRLF at the end of the response is sent to the client.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The initial connection must not be part of a pipeline; that is, the client MUST NOT send any command until it receives the CRLF at the end of the greeting.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client uses blocking system calls to send commands, it MUST ensure that the amount of text sent in pipelining does not cause a deadlock between transmission and reception.
actions: limit pipelined data volume to prevent transmission deadlock

statements.subject: client
statements.description: the MODE READER command may not be pipelined
actions: send MODE READER as a standalone command before reading server response; do not pipeline MODE READER with subsequent commands

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: For the purposes of this specification, articles are required to conform to the rules in this section, and clients and servers MUST correctly process any article received from the other that does so.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In order to meet the general requirements of NNTP, an article MUST NOT include the octet NUL, MUST NOT contain the octets LF and CR other than as part of a CRLF pair, and MUST end with a CRLF pair.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: This specification puts no further restrictions on the body; in particular, it MAY be empty.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: There MAY be more than one header line with the same name.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The content MUST NOT contain CRLF; it MAY be empty.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: There MUST still be some other octet between any two CRLF pairs in a header line.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Header lines SHOULD NOT be folded before the space after the colon that follows the header name and SHOULD include at least one octet other than %x09 or %x20 between CRLF pairs.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: However, if an article that fails to satisfy this requirement has been received from elsewhere, clients and servers MAY transfer it to each other without re-folding it.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The content of a header SHOULD be in UTF-8.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: However, if an implementation receives an article from elsewhere that uses octets in the range 128 to 255 in some other manner, it MAY pass it to a client or server without modification.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Therefore, implementations MUST be prepared to receive such headers, and data derived from them (e.g., in the responses from the OVER command, Section 8.3), and MUST NOT assume that they are always UTF-8.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Each article MUST have a unique message-id; two articles offered by an NNTP server MUST NOT have the same message-id.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: For the purposes of this specification, message-ids are opaque strings that MUST meet the following requirements:

statements.subject: message
statements.description: A message-id MUST begin with "<", end with ">", and MUST NOT contain the latter except at the end.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: A message-id MUST be between 3 and 250 octets in length.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: A message-id MUST NOT contain octets other than printable US-ASCII characters.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server does not have any way to determine a message-id from the article itself, it MUST synthesize one (this specification does not require that the article be changed as a result).

statements.subject: nntp
statements.description: The matches must be in the same order, and the whole string must be used in the match.

statements.subject: nntp
statements.description: It can match an empty string, but it cannot match a subsequence of a UTF-8 sequence that is not aligned to the character boundaries.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: An NNTP server or extension MAY extend the syntax or semantics of wildmats provided that all wildmats that meet the requirements of Section 4.1 have the meaning ascribed to them by Section 4.2.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: This command MUST NOT be pipelined.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: the server MUST not return any other generic response code.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Following a 400 or 502 response, the server MUST immediately close the connection.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST present an appropriate response code as a greeting to the client.
actions: send greeting response code to client

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server will accept further commands from the client including POST, the server MUST present a 200 greeting code.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server will accept further commands from the client, but the client is not authorized to post articles using the POST command, the server MUST present a 201 greeting code.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Otherwise, the server MUST present a 400 or 502 greeting code and then immediately close the connection.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: 400 SHOULD be used if the issue is only temporary (for example, because of load) and the client can expect to be able to connect successfully at some point in the future without making any changes.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: 502 MUST be used if the client is not permitted under any circumstances to interact with the server, and MAY be used if the server has insufficient information to determine whether the issue is temporary or permanent.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Therefore, clients SHOULD use the CAPABILITIES command (Section 5.2) rather than rely on this response.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: This command MAY be issued at any time; the server MUST NOT require it to be issued in order to make use of any capability.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The response generated by this command MAY change during a session because of other state information (which, in turn, may be changed by the effects of other commands or by external events).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST NOT list the same capability twice in the response, even with different arguments.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Except that the VERSION capability MUST be the first line, the order in which the capability lines appears is not significant; the server need not even consistently return the same order.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: An NNTP client MAY cache the results of this command, but MUST NOT rely on the correctness of any cached results, whether from earlier in this session or from a previous session, MUST cope gracefully with the cached status being out of date, and SHOULD (if caching results) provide a way to force the cached information to be refreshed.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Furthermore, a client MUST NOT use cached results in relation to security, privacy, and authentication extensions.
statements.pre_cond: client.capabilities_cached = true & (extension.type = security | extension.type = privacy | extension.type = authentication)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server does not recognise the argument (and it is a keyword), it MUST respond with the 101 response code as if the argument had been omitted.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If an argument is provided that the server does recognise, it MAY use the 101 response code or MAY use some other response code (which will be defined in the specification of that feature).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the argument is not a keyword, the 501 generic response code MUST be returned.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST NOT generate any other response code to the CAPABILITIES command.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Following a 502 response the server MUST immediately close the connection.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: It MUST then return a 200 or 201 response with the same meaning as for the initial greeting (as described in Section 5.1.1).
actions: switch from transit mode to reader mode

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MUST NOT issue MODE READER more than once in a session or after any security or privacy commands are issued.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When the MODE READER command is issued, the server MAY reset its state to that immediately after the initial connection before switching mode.
actions: reset state to that immediately after the initial connection

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If it advertises the READER capability, it MUST return a 200 or 201 response with the same meaning as for the initial greeting; in this case, the command MUST NOT affect the server state in any way.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If it does not advertise the READER capability, it MUST return a 502 response and then immediately close the connection.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Note that in both of these situations, the client SHOULD NOT use MODE READER.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST acknowledge the QUIT command and then close the connection to the client.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a client simply disconnects (or if the connection times out or some other fault occurs), the server MUST gracefully cease its attempts to service the client, disconnecting from its end if necessary.
actions: disconnect from server end if necessary

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST NOT generate any response code to the QUIT command other than 205 or, if any arguments are provided, 501.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: On a particular server, there MUST only be one article with a given number within any newsgroup, and an article MUST NOT have two different numbers in the same newsgroup.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: An article can be cross-posted to multiple newsgroups, so there may be multiple keys that point to the same article on the same server; these MAY have different numbers in each newsgroup.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: However, this type of key is not required to be globally unique, so the same key MAY refer to different articles on different servers.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST ensure that article numbers are issued in order of arrival timestamp; that is, articles arriving later MUST have higher numbers than those that arrive earlier.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server SHOULD allocate the next sequential unused number to each new article.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Article numbers MUST lie between 1 and 2,147,483,647, inclusive.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The client and server MAY use leading zeroes in specifying article numbers but MUST NOT use more than 16 digits.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: While servers MUST NOT send article numbers greater than this current limit, client and server developers are advised to use internal structures and datatypes capable of handling larger values in anticipation of such a change.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the group is not empty, the estimate MUST be at least the actual number of articles available and MUST be no greater than one more than the difference between the reported low and high water marks.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Clients MUST accept all three cases; servers MUST NOT represent an empty group in any other way.

statements.subject: server
